healthcare_biotech.rationale: Facts: the Democratic sweep gave Medicaid/ACA-exposed insurers and hospitals a sourced re-rating on Nov 4 (CNC +12.6%, MOH +8.9%, HCA +10.3%, UHS +10.9%, THC +9.6%) on expected delays to OBBBA Medicaid cuts and better ACA-subsidy odds. XLV acted as a defensive leader (ATH Nov 4, -2.5% vs SPY -4.4% on Nov 5, flat on the week), with biotech trading as rate-sensitive growth (XBI -6.7% Nov 5). Headwinds are slow and largely known: Medicare negotiation made permanent from 2029, GLP-1 negotiated prices from Jan 1, 2027, GLOBE MFN from Nov 30; JPM expects gridlock and lame-duck ACA/PBM status is unverified. Interpretation: mild tailwind, best expressed via broad XLV/VHT or providers rather than XBI; overlaps the defensive-factor rotation, so do not double count with us_factor_dividend.

industrials_defense_infra.rationale: Facts: both legs point negative. Defense: defense advocates lost seats (Collins, Kiggans), the likely FY27 topline is about $1.1T vs the ~$1.5T request, reconciliation odds were cut to ~10%, the CR expires Dec 11 (Callan 50% shutdown risk; Polymarket 31.5% by Dec 12), and NDAA/appropriations likely slip to 2027; LMT and LHX fell 6.9% on Nov 4. Data-centre build-out: GEV -7 to -11.5%, FIX -15.1%, PAVE -6.7% on the week, with Goldman and Morgan Stanley expecting project delays in Texas, Ohio and Georgia. Offsets: strong ISM (55.5), Iran-war munitions replenishment and a $67B supplemental support missile-defense primes, and signed backlogs cushion near-term earnings. Interpretation: -1 not -2; expect dispersion (missile-defense over platforms/shipbuilding) and treat the data-centre leg as part of the common AI-buildout factor.

utilities_realestate.rationale: Facts: merchant IPPs with Texas/data-centre exposure were hit hardest (VST -13.5 to -15%, CEG -8 to -9%) after Hinojosa won Texas on a data-centre approval moratorium, Ohio elected Acton (conditional moratorium) and voters rejected data centres in 40 of 41 local measures; KeyBanc downgraded VST. Rates add a second headwind: Dec 9 hike odds about 70-78% after +165k payrolls. Offsets: Vistra beat and raised (2027 EBITDA guide $7.7-8.5B, ~98% hedged, new 207 MW Texas PPA), Entergy reported higher data-centre sales, no source says the moratorium reaches signed ERCOT agreements, it cannot start before Jan 19 and statute needs a 19-12 GOP Senate; the 10y fell to ~4.86% from 5.24%, XLRE/VNQ rose ~0.8% while XLU fell ~0.7%, and regulated renewables (NEE +4.6%) gained. Interpretation: mild headwind concentrated in IPPs; -2 only if the moratorium targets signed interconnection agreements or the December ERCOT audit brings clawbacks.

clean_energy_thematic.rationale: Facts: renewables rallied on Nov 4 (ENPH +8.8%, FSLR +8.4%, RUN +6.9%, NEE +4.6%) but the rally reversed into a sharp sell-off on Nov 5 and ICLN sits >30% below end-May. Analysts (Morningstar, PV Tech Research) say 'for solar, nothing changes': the lame duck is still Republican, credit-restoration bills lapse Jan 3, Democrats lack 60 Senate votes and a veto override. Reported fundamentals are weak: First Solar cut FY26 guidance (Oct 29), Enphase guided Q4 far below consensus with sell-through -35% (Oct 28), Sunrun cut its cash-generation guide, Orsted took a DKK 3.4bn rate-driven US impairment while keeping guidance and reaching Revolution Wind COD. The Section 232 15% tariff plus $0.38/W module floor starts Dec 4, raising installer costs (relative positive only for FSLR), and a December Fed hike is likely. Interpretation: this revises round 0's +1 down: the pop was a policy-relief squeeze from a depressed base, not a re-rating; mean reversion likely over 1-3 months.

regime_notes: The Nov 3 Democratic sweep reshuffled sectors on Nov 4: managed care, hospitals, homebuilders, airlines and renewables rallied while defense, merchant power and data-centre capex names sold off. Most of the policy effect lands after the 1-3 month window (Congress seats Jan 3, Hinojosa Jan 19, Acton budget Mar 15); inside the window the binding items are the Dec 11 CR expiry (defense, ACA subsidies, PBM riders and clean-energy credits ride the same vehicle), the mid-December ERCOT data-centre audit, the Dec 4 Section 232 solar tariff and the Dec 9 FOMC. The utilities IPP leg and the industrials data-centre leg belong to the same AI-buildout factor that drove SOX -12% on Nov 5, so they should not be counted as independent negatives. Healthcare's strength overlaps the defensive/quality rotation (XLP, XLV, SPLV, SCHD ATHs on Nov 4). Rates remain the shared driver for utilities, REITs and clean energy: the 10y rallied to ~4.86% as oil fell, but Dec hike odds are ~70-78%, and Oct CPI on Nov 10 (Cleveland core nowcast 0.21%) is the key swing input. A US strike on Iran would reverse the oil-driven relief that helped airlines and rate-sensitive sectors.
